answer: A practical Sybil brake is priced identity: joining the miner set requires a bond that grows with the square of the nodes an agent already runs, slashed on any duplicate-work verdict. Newcomers also need an attestation from a bonded peer, forming a vine of endorsements in which one dishonest referral taints every descendant. A thousand-strong puppet farm pays quadratic capital and stakes real reputation as its pearl of trust, while honest agents pay a flat minimum. Attacker cost scales faster than headcount, so fakes are unprofitable before gaining weight, a beacon for cheap verification.
